name: Humboldt and Bonpland in the Americas
traveler: Alexander von Humboldt and Aimé Bonpland
summary: A Prussian naturalist and a French botanist carry 42 instruments through the Spanish Americas, measuring altitude, temperature, magnetism and plants as they go. They show how climate and life change with height, and their thirty-volume account remakes Europe's picture of South America.

stops.note: Sail on the Pizarro with royal permission to go anywhere in Spanish America.
Climb the volcano and record how vegetation changes with height.
Experiments with electric eels on the grassy plains.
Confirm that the Casiquiare joins the Orinoco to the Amazon basin.
Studies the cinchona trees that give quinine.
Climbs the volcanoes around the city.
Reach about 5,900 metres, higher than anyone known before them; from it Humboldt draws his famous profile of life by altitude.
Measure the cold current offshore, later named after Humboldt.
A year in New Spain's archives and mines.
Meets President Jefferson, who wants news of Mexico's borders.
Home with 60,000 specimens; publishing takes thirty years.
